title: A new approach to strong convergence

source.citation: Ramon van Handel, The strong convergence phenomenon (survey, Current Developments in Mathematics 2025; arXiv 2507.00346), presenting the method of Chen, Garza-Vargas, Tropp, van Handel, A new approach to strong convergence (Ann. Math. 2026; arXiv 2405.16026)
source.scope: proof of Friedman's theorem via the polynomial method (master inequality for polynomials, extension to smooth functions); also 2405.16026 Sections on random regular graphs
source.evidence: README: "We hope to formalize this new proof, following van Handel's survey (https://web.math.princeton.edu/~rvan/cdm250630.pdf)" and cites Chen-Garza-Vargas-Tropp-van Handel arXiv 2405.16026; blueprint cites chen2025. The survey cdm250630.pdf matches arXiv 2507.00346 (survey for CDM 2025, 75 pp.).

edge_sample.source_text: lemma : Let $x, y \in V(G)$. Then \begin{equation*} \langle a \mathbf{1}_{\{x\}}, \mathbf{1}_{\{y\}} \rangle = \# \mathrm{dartSet}(x,y). \end{equation*}
edge_sample.target_text: proof : By Lemma \ref{lem:coefficients_adjacency_expression}, this quantity is a cardinal of a set, and hence a non-negative integer. The parity when $x=y$ comes from Lemma \ref{lem:darset_loop_even}.

edge_sample.source_text: definition : Let $x \in V(G)$ and $r \in \mathbb{N}$. We define the \emph{ball $B_r(x)$ of radius $r$ centered at $x$} as the set of vertices $y \in V(G)$ such that $\mathrm{edist}(x,y)\leq r$.
edge_sample.target_text: lemma : Assume $G$ is a graph of finite diameter. For any $x \in V(G)$, $V(G)$ is included in the ball of radius $\mathrm{diam}(G)$ centered at $x$.

edge_sample.source_text: lemma : Let $x, y \in V(G)$. Then \begin{equation*} \langle a \mathbf{1}_{\{x\}}, \mathbf{1}_{\{y\}} \rangle = \# \mathrm{dartSet}(x,y). \end{equation*}
edge_sample.target_text: lemma : For any $x, y \in V(G)$, $\langle a \mathbf{1}_{\{x\}}, \mathbf{1}_{\{y\}} \rangle$ is a non-negative integer, which is even as soon as $x=y$.

edge_sample.source_text: definition : We define a binary relation on $V(G)$ by: $x \sim y$ if there exists a dartwalk from $x$ to $y$ on $G$. We then say $x$ and $y$ are \emph{reachable}.
edge_sample.target_text: lemma : Let $f : V(G) \rightarrow \mathbb{C}$ be a locally constant function. For any $x, y \in V(G)$, if $x$ and $y$ are reachable, then $f(x)=f(y)$.

edge_sample.target_text: proposition : The homotopy relation is an equivalence relation.

edge_sample.source_text: definition : Let $(G,r)$ be a rooted graph. Let $x \in V(G)$. A vertex $y \in V(G)$ is a \emph{parent} of $x$ if $y$ is adjacent to $x$ and $\mathrm{dist}(r,y) = \mathrm{dist}(r,x)-1$.
edge_sample.target_text: lemma : Let $(G,r)$ be a rooted graph. Assume $G$ is connected. Any vertex $x \in V(G)$ distinct from the root admits a parent.
